observations: Torah LM2 #64 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — three sentences. It presents a single explanatory argument: the madness (שִׁגָּעוֹן) of wealthy leaders (נְגִידִים) is caused by money (מָמוֹן), which in turn derives from the fallen wealth (נְפִילַת הָעֲשִׁירוּת) of the prophets, whose prophetic ecstasy expressed itself as apparent madness. The requirement for a new package is that 3+ concepts be connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This Torah does not meet that threshold: (1) No explicit 'בְּחִינַת' language appears anywhere in the three sentences; (2) all connections between concepts are causal (eitza) — money 'makes' (עוֹשֶׂה) one mad, the wealth 'derives from' (מִנְּפִילַת) the prophets; (3) there is no independent conceptual cluster built through parallel-nature equations. The teaching is a complete causal explanation but not a bechina network. No new package is warranted.
